'''Jeffree David Withey''' (born March 7, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Pelita Jaya Basketball Club|Pelita Jaya Jakarta]] of the [[Indonesian Basketball League]] (IBL). He played college basketball for the [[University of Kansas]] where he became known for his shot-blocking ability and his defensive presence.<ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3818&path=mbball|work=kuathletics.com|access-date=December 22, 2013|title=Jeff Withey - 2012-13 Men's Basketball}}</ref> He was drafted 39th overall in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref name="draft">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-cj-mccollum-jeff-withey-marko-todorovic-and-draft-rights-allen-crabbe-201|title=Trail Blazers Acquire C.J. McCollum, Jeff Withey, Marko Todorovic And Draft Rights To Allen Crabbe In 2013 NBA Draft|date=June 27, 2013|website=nba.com|language=en|access-date=May 21, 2017}}</ref>

==High school career==
Withey led Horizon High School to the state Division IV title in his sophomore season (2006) <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/uniontrib/20061102/news_1s2p-notes.html|title=Horizon 7-footer chooses Louisville for basketball|publisher=Union-Tribune Publishing Co.|year=2006}}</ref> and he graduated in the class of 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=1947382|title=Scout: Jeff Withey|publisher=Microsoft|year=2012}}</ref> In the game preceding the state championship game, Withey and his teammates had to face a [[San Joaquin Memorial High School]] team in the Southern California Regional Championship game that featured three seniors who were future NBA players, [[Robin Lopez|Robin]] & [[Brook Lopez]] and [[Quincy Pondexter]]. In a dramatic double-overtime game, Withey and his teammates overcame the San Joaquin squad and went on to win the title in the following game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/contests/mBbA_N82pUy_dtA9VNRnow/basketball-winter-05-06/boxscore-horizon-san-diego-vs-san-joaquin-memorial-fresno.htm|title=Horizon edges San Joaquin Memorial|publisher=Maxpreps|year=2006}}</ref>

In his senior season he averaged 20.8 points, 13.0 rebounds, and 7.3 blocked shots per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/03/25/sports/ncaabasketball/jeff-withey-of-kansas-is-a-shot-blocker-supreme.html|title=Kansas Center's Reach Has Foes Grasping at Straws|publisher=The New York Times Company|year=2012}}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Withey was listed as the No. 8 center and the No. 36 player in the nation in 2008.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Jeff-Withey-47100;_ylt=AhJf.KLWWVzQ3pQiMv3qGvJGPZB4 Jeff Withey Recruiting profile]</ref>

==College career==

===Arizona (2008)===
Withey had originally committed to play for Louisville, but switched his commitment to Arizona. Following the resignation of [[Lute Olson]] in October of Withey's freshman season, he decided to transfer from Arizona. He did not see any playing time for the Wildcats during his semester of the 2008–09 season.

===Kansas (2009–2013)===
[[File:Jeff Withey 2013.jpg|thumb|upright|right|Jeff Withey in June 2013]]
Withey transferred to Kansas in January 2009, but was ineligible to play until the end of the 2009 fall semester due to the NCAA transfer rules requiring him to sit out a year. He initially saw limited playing time during the second half of the 2009–10 season and the 2010–11 season, playing behind [[Cole Aldrich]] and the Morris twins.

In his [[2011–12 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|junior year]], after twin brothers [[Marcus Morris (basketball)|Marcus]] and [[Markieff Morris]] left for the [[2011 NBA Draft|NBA draft]], he became a starter,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/andy_glockner/04/02/Kansas.Jeff.Withey/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120404213356/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/andy_glockner/04/02/Kansas.Jeff.Withey/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 4, 2012|title=Withey could be difference maker as Kansas looks to upset Kentucky|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=April 2, 2012}}</ref> playing for the 2011–12 squad which lost to Kentucky in the NCAA championship game.  Withey blocked 31 shots in the 2012 tournament, breaking [[Joakim Noah]]'s tournament record of 29.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kansascity.com/2012/04/02/3532103/no-joy-in-block-record-for-withey.html|title=No joy in block record for Withey|publisher=Kansas City Star|date=April 2, 2012}}</ref> During the 2011–12 season, he was named [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] defensive player of the year and set a Big 12 record with 140 blocks for the season.<ref name="LJW04Oct12" />

====2012–13 season====
On October 4, 2012, Withey was named to the Preseason [[Big 12 Conference|all-Big 12]] unanimously.<ref name="LJW04Oct12">[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2012/oct/04/jeff-withey-named-preseason-all-big-12-elijah-john/?mens_basketball Jeff Withey named to preseason all-Big 12; Elijah Johnson honorable mention], Lawrence Journal-World, October 4, 2012.</ref>

On December 3, 2012, Withey was named Big 12 Player of the Week.  To earn the honor, he scored a [[triple-double]] against [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State Spartans]] on November 26. In that game, Withey scored 16 points, grabbed 12 rebounds, and blocked 12 shots, for the second triple-double in KU history.<ref>[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2012/dec/03/jeff-withey-wins-big-12-player-week/?mens_basketball Jeff Withey wins Big 12 player of week], [[Lawrence Journal-World]], December 3, 2012.</ref> On February 18, 2013, Withey was named Big 12 Co-Player of the Week.  He had [[double-double]]s against both [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]].  He also made his 265th blocked shot to set a new Big 12 record for career blocked shots.<ref>[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2013/feb/18/kansas-center-jeff-withey-shares-big-12-player-wee/?mens_basketball Kansas center Jeff Withey shares Big 12 player of the week honors], [[Lawrence Journal-World]], February 18, 2013.</ref>

Withey finished his senior year of college by averaging 13.7 points, 8.5 rebounds and 3.9 blocks.<ref>Dodd, Rustin. [http://www.kansascity.com/2013/06/28/4318189/portland-takes-withey.html Portland drafts KU's Jeff Withey with 39th overall pick], ''[[Kansas City Star]]'', June 28, 2013.</ref>

On March 10, 2013, he was named defensive player of the year in the Big 12 for 2012–13 and he was named first team All Big 12.<ref>{{Cite web  | last = Bedore | first = Gary | title = Jeff Withey, Ben McLemore selected to All-Big 12 first team | url = http://www2.kusports.com/news/2013/mar/10/kansas-center-jeff-withey-named-big-12-defensive-p/?mens_basketball | publisher = KUsports.com | date = March 10, 2013 | access-date = March 11, 2013 }}</ref>  On March 11, 2013, Withey was named 2nd Team [[All-American]] by The Sporting News.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Keeley |first=Laura |title=Seth Curry named Sporting News All-American |url=http://blogs.newsobserver.com/dukenow/seth-curry-all-american |publisher=newsobserver.com |date=March 11, 2013 |access-date=March 13, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130629035549/http://blogs.newsobserver.com/dukenow/seth-curry-all-american |archive-date=June 29, 2013 }}</ref>  On March 31, 2013, Withey was accorded third-team All-American mention by the [[Associated Press]].<ref>Bedore, Gary. [http://www2.kusports.com/news/2013/apr/01/ben-mclemore-earns-second-team-ap-all-america-hono/?mens_basketball KU freshman Ben McLemore earns All-America honors], ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]]'', April 1, 2013</ref>

On April 5, 2013, the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] named Withey the [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year|co-National Defensive Player of the Year]].

==Professional career==

===New Orleans Pelicans (2013–2015)===
Withey was selected with the 39th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref name="draft" /> He was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in a three-team trade involving the Trail Blazers and the [[Sacramento Kings]] on July 10, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=NEW ORLEANS PELICANS ACQUIRE TYREKE EVANS AND JEFF WITHEY IN THREE-TEAM TRADE|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-tyreke-evans-and-jeff-withey-three-team-trade|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=July 23, 2013}}</ref> In two seasons for the Pelicans, he averaged 3.0 points and 2.3 rebounds in 95 games.

===Utah Jazz (2015–2017)===
On August 24, 2015, Withey signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-jeff-withey-multi-year-contract|title=Jazz Sign Jeff Withey to Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|date=August 24, 2015|access-date=August 24, 2015}}</ref> On December 28, 2015, he recorded a season-high 11 points and a career-high 12 rebounds as a starter in a 95–91 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151228/PHIUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Gordon Hayward scores 24, Jazz beats 76ers 95-91|work=NBA.com|date=December 28, 2015|access-date=December 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151227034038/http://www.nba.com/games/20151228/PHIUTA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 27, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2017)===
On August 21, 2017, Withey signed a one-year deal with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-center-jeff-withey/|title=Mavs sign center Jeff Withey|work=mavs.com|date=August 21, 2017|access-date=August 21, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on December 19, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mavericks sign Kyle Collinsworth to two-way contract|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-kyle-collinsworth-two-way-contract/|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 19, 2017|date=December 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222052040/https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-kyle-collinsworth-two-way-contract/|archive-date=December 22, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Tofaş (2018)===
On July 24, 2018, Withey signed with the Turkish team [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] for the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tofas Bursa signs Jeff Withey|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/283223/tofas-bursa-signs-jeff-withey.html|work=Sportando.basketball|access-date=July 24, 2018|date=July 24, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180724154154/https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/283223/tofas-bursa-signs-jeff-withey.html|archive-date=July 24, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 28, 2018, Withey parted ways with Tofaş after appearing in 19 games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tofas, Jeff Withey part ways|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/tofas-jeff-withey-part-ways/|work=Sportando.basketball|access-date=December 29, 2018|date=December 28, 2018|archive-date=September 19, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210919200042/https://sportando.basketball/en/tofas-jeff-withey-part-ways/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Lavrio (2019)===
On February 28, 2019, Withey signed with Greek team [[G.S. Lavrio B.C.|Lavrio]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jeff Withey signs with Lavrio|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jeff-withey-signs-with-lavrio/|work=Sportando.basketball|access-date=August 18, 2019|date=February 28, 2019|archive-date=February 1, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230201014135/https://sportando.basketball/en/jeff-withey-signs-with-lavrio/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 30, 2019, Withey recorded a season-high 18 points, shooting 8-of-10 from the field, along with six rebounds and two blocks in an 88–99 loss to [[P.A.O.K. BC|PAOK]].<ref>{{cite web|title=GS Lavrio 88 at PAOK BC 99|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-03-30/GS-Lavrio-at-PAOK-BC/330754|work=RealGM.com|access-date=August 18, 2019|date=March 30, 2019}}</ref> In 10 games played for Lavrio, he averaged 6.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.5 blocks per game.

On July 4, 2019, Withey joined the [[Washington Wizards]] for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards announce 2019 Summer League roster|url=https://www.bulletsforever.com/2019/7/4/20681425/washington-wizards-2019-summer-league-roster-rui-hachimura-admiral-schofield-troy-brown-issuf-sanon|work=BulletsForever.com|access-date=August 18, 2019|date=July 4, 2019}}</ref>

===Ironi Nes Ziona (2019–2020)===
On August 18, 2019, Withey signed a one-year deal with [[Ironi Nes Ziona B.C.|Ironi Nes Ziona]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=וויטי יהיה השחקן הגבוה בתולדות נס ציונה|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=22496|work=basket.co.il|access-date=August 18, 2019|date=August 18, 2019|language=he}}</ref> On October 23, 2019, Withey recorded a double-double of 23 points and 11 rebounds, leading Nes Ziona to an 82–75 win over the [[Kapfenberg Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kapfenberg Bulls v Ironi Ness Ziona boxscore - FIBA Europe Cup 2019-20|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/19-20/game/2310/Kapfenberg-Bulls-Ironi-Ness-Ziona|work=FIBA.Basketball|access-date=November 11, 2019|date=October 23, 2019}}</ref> He was subsequently named Europe Cup round 1 Top Performer.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jeff Withey lands Top Performer honors with double-double in winning start for Ironi Ness Ziona|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/19-20/news/jeff-withey-lands-top-performer-honors-with-double-double-in-winning-start-for-ironi-ness-ziona|work=FIBA.Basketball|access-date=November 11, 2019|date=October 24, 2019}}</ref> On December 5, 2019, Withey was named [[2019–20 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Player of the Month|Israeli League Player of the Month]] after averaging a double-double of 16.3 points and 13.3 rebounds, while shooting 66 percent from the field in eight games played in November.<ref>{{cite news|title=שחקן חודש נובמבר בליגת ווינר סל: ג'ף וויטי|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=22854|work=basket.co.il|access-date=December 5, 2019|date=December 5, 2019|language=he}}</ref> On December 23, 2019, Withey recorded a new career-high 24 points, while shooting 10-of-12 from the field, along with seven rebounds and three steals in a 95–80 win over [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Winner League, Game 11: Nes Ziona Vs Hapoel TA|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24082&lang=en|work=basket.co.il|access-date=December 23, 2019|date=December 23, 2019}}</ref>

===Goyang Orion Orions (2020–2021)===
On July 8, 2020, Withey signed with the [[Goyang Orion Orions]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=위디와 로슨 영입한 강을준 감독 “높이 약한 팀 상황 고려한 선택” |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065610837065807 |website=점프볼 |access-date=February 19, 2025 |date=July 8, 2020}}</ref> On February 3, 2021, he was replaced by [[Devin Williams (basketball)|Devin Williams]].<ref>{{cite web |title=오리온, 새 외국선수 데빈 윌리엄스 등록 완료...3일 LG 전 출전 가능 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065601060559296 |website=점프볼 |access-date=February 19, 2025 |date=February 3, 2021}}</ref> He averaged 8.8 points and 7.3 rebounds per game in the Korean Basketball League.<ref name="bilbao" />

===Bilbao Basket (2021–2023)===
On July 21, 2021, Withey signed with [[Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref name="bilbao">{{cite web |title=RETAbet Bilbao announces Jeff Withey |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/retabet-bilbao-announces-jeff-withey/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=July 21, 2021}}</ref>

On August 22, 2023, he signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-tel-aviv-inks-jeff-withey/|title=Hapoel Tel Aviv inks Jeff Withey|last=|first=|date=August 22, 2023|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 23, 2023}}</ref> However, he never played for the team.

===Wonju DB Promy (2023–2024)===
On October 29, 2023, Withey signed with the [[Wonju DB Promy]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] to replace [[Garrison Brooks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=‘DB 2옵션’ 제프 위디, 외국선수 등록 마쳐···3일 가스공사전 출전 가능 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065592595062222 |website=점프볼 |access-date=February 19, 2025 |date=November 3, 2023}}</ref>

===Taipei Fubon Braves (2024–present)===
On August 26, 2024, Withey signed with the [[Taipei Fubon Braves]] of the [[P. League+]].<ref>{{cite web |title=富邦勇士簽下第4位洋將威希！共有5年NBA經歷 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2804561 |website=ETtoday運動雲 |access-date=February 19, 2025 |date=August 26, 2024}}</ref>
